summary: The Stop China’s Exploitation of Congolese Children and Adult Forced Labor through Cobalt Mining Act requires the federal Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force to investigate forced and child labor in the cobalt mining industry of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Within 180 days of enactment, the task force must deliver a report and enforcement strategy to Congress detailing how to prevent cobalt mined by forced labor from entering the United States market, including through third countries. The bill also mandates semiannual briefings to Congress and outlines that these requirements will end after eight years or once the President determines that forced labor in the DRC mining industry has ended.

affected_groups.effect: Must complete the required investigation, formulate enforcement and traceability strategies, consult with agencies and non-governmental entities, and provide ongoing semiannual briefings to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force and Federal Agencies

affected_groups.effect: Subject to stricter enforcement strategies, tracing requirements, and potential import restrictions or bans on cobalt and related products tied to forced labor in the DRC.

key_provisions: Requires the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force to complete and submit an investigation regarding forced labor in the DRC cobalt mining industry within 180 days of enactment.
Directs the task force to create strategies to prevent the import of forced-labor cobalt into the U.S., including cobalt entering via third countries or re-entering after being denied entry.
Requires the investigation to include a list of entities in the DRC potentially using forced labor for cobalt and a list of priority downstream product sectors containing DRC cobalt.
Mandates recommendations for tools, technologies, and traceability measures to help U.S. Customs and Border Protection identify and trace forced-labor cobalt.
Requires the task force to provide semiannual briefings to appropriate congressional committees on strategy updates and enforcement actions.
Establishes a sunset clause ending the act's requirements after eight years or when the President determines forced labor in the DRC mining industry has ended.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Stop China’s Exploitation of Congolese Children and Adult Forced Labor through Cobalt Mining Act requires the federal Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force to investigate forced and child labor in the cobalt mining industry of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Within 180 days of enactment, the task force must deliver a report and enforcement strategy to Congress detailing how to prevent cobalt mined by forced labor from entering the United States market, including through third countries. The bill also mandates semiannual briefings to Congress and outlines that these requirements will end after eight years or once the President determines that forced labor in the DRC mining industry has ended.
summary_detail.significance: The bill directs federal attention and investigative resources toward blocking cobalt extracted through forced and child labor in the DRC from entering American supply chains. It mandates specific oversight, reporting, and tracing mechanisms for industries reliant on lithium-ion batteries and other electronic components, operating under a sunset period of up to eight years.
